title: Elastic Commitment Barter — PRD sketch
body:
Purpose
This is a lightweight PRD sketch for the Elastic Commitment Barter: a runtime+control-plane mechanism that lets tenants temporarily trade (lend/borrow) small slices of reserved GPU capacity across committed pools in exchange for credits. The aim is to reduce wasted reserved capacity during idleness while preserving isolation and SLOs.

Context / problem we're solving
- Many committed pools are sized for peak seasonal usage; a lot of capacity sits underutilized.
- Tenants want predictable tail latency and reserved throughput (SLOs) but also want cheaper operations when their traffic is low.
- Existing burst mechanisms either strictly isolate or allow blunt overcommit with poor fairness.
- Ops team spends time resolving contention and manual tenant carve-outs.

High-level goals (what success looks like)
- Reduce average unused reserved GPU time across dedicated fleet by >= 20% for participating pools.
- Maintain tenant-visible latency SLOs for primary reserved lanes; any borrowed capacity must not violate pre-agreed latency targets for lenders.
- Provide transparent accounting and an auditable credit ledger so finance/CS can bill or refund credit transfers.
- Allow safe automated reversion: lenders can withdraw offered capacity within pre-defined safety windows.

Non‑goals
- This does not replace hard preemption for critical production tenants.
- Not a full marketplace; initial iteration limited to intra-organization or committed-customer pairs.

Core idea / design sketch
1) Commitment units and credit model
   - Define a Commitment Unit (CU): abstract unit mapping to a normalized GPU concurrency/time slice (e.g., 0.1 of an RTX-X for 1 hour).
   - Tenants buy or reserve CUs as part of Dedicated contracts. Unused CU time accrues as "lendable" budget.
   - Borrowers can request short-lived CU leases (minutes–hours) in exchange for credits. Price is dynamic: base price + surge multiplier + lender incentive.

2) Broker + match engine (control plane)
   - Broker receives borrow requests specifying: CU amount, max price, max duration, latency tier required, region, model family affinity.
   - Matching only occurs between compatible lenders (region, hardware, model delta tolerance).
   - Policy layer enforces lender protection: guarantee a fraction of lender pool remains unborrowed (headroom fraction) and a retraction buffer (warmup/wakeup time).

3) Runtime enforcement and isolation
   - When lender offers CU to borrower, runtime creates isolated slice: cgroup-like GPU scheduling or slot reservation with QoS tags.
   - Borrowed workloads run with lower priority and can be throttled before lender SLOs are impacted. Throttling policy: proportional backoff, token-bucket burst window, then eviction.
   - KV-cache locality and model warm caches are not shared across tenants: borrowing creates separate execution contexts to avoid cross-tenant contamination.

4) Safety & graceful fallback
   - Lender signal: if lender traffic grows above threshold, broker auto-reclaims borrowed CUs with a configurable grace window (30s-5m). Borrower gets an ETA and fallback model route (e.g., lower-cost hosted model or queued requests).
   - Circuit breaker: if reclamation frequently happens for a pair, reduce matching weight and increase lender reserve fraction.

5) Accounting & visibility
   - Credit ledger records: lender id, borrower id, CU amount, start/end, price, reclaimed events. Ledger exported to billing nightly.
   - Console: per-tenant view of lent/borrowed history, realtime borrow utilization heatmap, and projected savings.

Operational scenarios / examples (short)
- Scenario A: Small SaaS tenant with 50% idleness during US night offers 10 CU to the pool for 3 hours; a neighbor bursty tenant borrows them for a price that nets lender 30% off monthly commitment.
- Scenario B: Lender unexpected surge — broker retracts 8 CU within 60s; borrower fallback routes 20% of requests to hosted API and queues the rest. Billing shows partial refund for reclaimed minutes.

Metrics to track (prototype)
- Utilization delta on participating pools (pre/post).
- Fraction of reclaims per borrow (target < 5%).
- Average borrower request tail latency during borrow windows vs baseline.
- Revenue/credit flow and net savings for lenders.

Simulation plan
- Build a discrete-event simulator that models: pool sizes, baseline arrival processes for tenants, lender lending policies, borrow matching latency, warmup/wakeup, and reclamation.
- Run multi-week traces using production-sampled traffic patterns (ask SRE to share anonymized traces: JIRA-DED-2109).
- Sensitivity sweeps across headroom_fraction (0.05–0.4), grace_window (30s–5m), and price elasticity.

APIs and UX (initial)
- API: POST /dedicated/borrow-requests {tenant_id, region, CU_amount, max_price, duration, latency_tier} -> request_id
- API: GET /dedicated/lending-offers/{tenant_id} -> list of active offers, expected price
- Console: "Enable lending" toggle per-reservation with sliders: max_lend_pct, min_headroom, price_floor.

Risks & open questions
- Model warm/cold effects: lending may force borrower to pay warmup cost; is lender compensated for downstream cache-warm assistance? (probably no, but needs discussion)
- Security/regulatory: do we need stricter isolation for regulated tenants? Might restrict who can lend/borrow.
- Billing complexity and refunds on frequent reclamations. Need finance input on rounding/credits.
- SRE operational overhead: can this be automated enough to avoid paging? What observability hooks required?

Next steps / runbook for MVP
- Week 0–2: mock up protocol + pricing rules; align with finance and CS (owners: Claire + Ravi).
- Week 3–6: implement simulator and run on 3 sample pools; share results with engineering and SRE.
- Week 7–12: runtime prototype: minimal broker, reservation tagging, and conservative headroom defaults (0.3). Pilot with 2 friendly customers.
- Deliverables: simulator report, API draft, pilot playbook, and a Postmortem template for reclamation incidents.

Notes to self / loose ideas
- Could extend to cross-org marketplace later but needs strong trust + SLA primitives.
- Consider incentivizing long loans (multi-hour) with discounts rather than minute-by-minute.
- Add a "dry-run" mode to show projected lender earnings without actually moving capacity.

Links / refs
- Related drive notes: shared_drives/product/dedicated/predictive-warm-pool-orchestrator-and-borrowing-prd-draft.json (for warm-pool ideas)
- Slack thread: #dedicated-burst (pin: lender-price-proposal)

End of sketch.
